requirements.text: The rear lighting assembly shall be so designed and constructed that its satisfactory operation remains assured in normal conditions of use, including the vibrations to which it is subjected.

Where the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp, the two functions shall be provided by multiple light sources or the lamp shall be intended for use on a vehicle equipped with a failure tell-tale.
The rear position and stop functions incorporated in a common housing shall be provided by multiple light sources, for instance a double filament light source.
Where a vehicle manufacturer logo is incorporated in the lens, the enclosed light emitting surface of the logo in the direction of the reference axis shall not exceed 100 cm2.
The stop lamp and the rear direction indicator lamp shall not incorporate a manufacturer logo in their apparent surface.
In a single lamp of the assembly containing more than one light source, a group wired so that failure of any one causes all to extinguish shall be considered one light source.

Where any one light source fails in a single lamp containing more than one light source, the lamp shall meet the minimum intensity requirement of the standard light distribution and not exceed the maximum intensities when all sources are illuminated, or produce a failure tell-tale signal.

With one light source failed, the light intensity shall comply with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of Annex 3, and with all light sources illuminated the maximum intensities shall not be exceeded.
For the rear direction indicator lamp of category 12, a signal for activation of the direction indicator failure tell-tale shall be produced on the basis of one of the options a), b) or c).

For the direction indicator lamp designed with only two light sources, the failure signal shall be produced when the intensity in the axis of reference falls below 50 per cent of the minimum intensity required.
The rear registration plate lamp shall be exempt from the single-light-source failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.1.2., while paragraph 4.6.1.1. remains applicable.

The stop lamp and rear position lamp for the L5e vehicle shall not be required to produce the failure tell-tale signal of paragraph 4.6.1.2. (b), but shall still meet paragraphs 4.6.1.1. and 4.6.1.2. (a).

Where the variable intensity control of a variable-intensity rear position lamp, stop lamp or direction indicator fails, the requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective steady category shall be fulfilled automatically.
The rear lighting assembly shall be equipped only with approved replaceable light sources, light source modules or non-replaceable light sources.
Where replaceable light sources are used, they shall be approved according to UN Regulations Nos. 37, 99 and/or 128 with no restriction on use at the time of application.
Where replaceable UN approved light sources are used, the lamp shall be designed such that each light source can be fixed in no other position but the correct one.
The rear lighting assembly shall not generate radiated or power line disturbances which cause a malfunction of other electrical or electronic systems of the vehicle.
Where a replaceable light source module is used, it shall be designed so that it can only be fitted in the designated and correct position and only removed with the use of tools.
The replaceable light source module of the assembly shall be tamperproof.
When the light source module is replaced by another module from the applicant bearing the same identification code, the photometric requirements of the device shall still be met.

Where replaceable light sources are controlled by electronic control gear, the standard light source shall have a luminous flux not deviating more than 5 per cent from the reference value when test voltage is applied.
During photometric measurements of the assembly, stray reflections shall be avoided by appropriate masking.

Where the lamp may be installed in more than one position, the photometric measurements shall be repeated for each position or for the extreme positions of the reference axis field specified by the manufacturer.
The measuring equipment for the assembly shall have an angular aperture of the receiver between 10' and 1 degree as viewed from the reference centre.
Unless otherwise specified, the lamp shall be tested with a supply voltage of 13.5 V for the 12 V vehicle electrical system.
The intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples on the reference axis shall be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function.
The intensity of light emitted by each sample shall not exceed, in any direction where the lamp is visible, the maximum specified in the table of the pertinent function.

Where the additional test is requested, the red light emitted by the rear lamp towards the front shall have a maximum intensity of not more than 2.5·10-1 cd in the angular field from 165° to 180° outboard and -2.5° to +5° vertical.

Where the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp, the ratio between the intensities measured with both lit and with the position lamp alone shall be at least 5:1 within the field bounded by ±5° V and ±10° H.
The colour of the light emitted by each function of the assembly shall be measured inside the light distribution grid field defined for that specific function.
Outside the light distribution field, no sharp variation of colour shall be observed on the lens of the assembly.
Where a function of the assembly uses different light source technologies, the colorimetric characteristics shall be checked separately for each technology.
For the rear position lamp reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp, a luminous intensity of 6.0·101 cd shall be permitted below a plane forming an angle of 5° downward from the horizontal.
The rear position lamp of category MR shall emit a minimum luminous intensity of 4·100 cd and a maximum of 1.7·101 cd as a single lamp.
The colour of light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.
The stop lamp for the category L vehicle (MS) shall emit a minimum luminous intensity of 4.0·101 cd and a maximum of 2.60·102 cd as a single lamp.
For the stop lamp pair (MS), the standard light distribution may be considered from the VV line to the outboard only, at the request of the applicant.
The colour of light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
The rear direction indicator lamp of category 12 shall emit a minimum luminous intensity of 5.0·101 cd and a maximum of 5.00·102 cd as a single lamp.
Where the direction indicator lamp is measured in flashing mode, it shall be switched at f = 1.5 ± 0.5 Hz with a pulse width greater than 0.3 s measured at 95 per cent peak light intensity.
Where sequential activation of light sources is used for the rear direction indicator, each light source shall remain lit until the end of the ON cycle.
The sequential activation shall produce a signal proceeding in a uniform progressive manner from the inboard towards the outboard edge of the light emitting surface.
Where sequential activation is used, the variation shall finish no more than 200 ms after the beginning of the ON cycle.
The orthogonal projection of the light emitting surfaces of the direction indicator shall be circumscribed by a rectangle whose horizontal to vertical side ratio is not less than 1.7.
The colour of light emitted by the rear direction indicator lamp shall be amber.
Where the registration plate lamp is approved to category 2, it shall illuminate an area of at least 200 x 280 mm for use on the category L vehicle.
At each measurement point of the illuminated area of category 1 or 2, the luminance shall be at least 2·100 cd/m².
The gradient of luminance between any two measurement points on the illuminated plate area shall not exceed 2 x Bo/cm, Bo being the minimum luminance measured.
The luminance of the registration plate lamp shall be measured on a diffuse colourless surface with a known diffuse reflection factor placed in the position normally occupied by the plate.
Luminance measurements shall be made perpendicularly to the diffuse surface, with a tolerance of 5° in each direction, at the points shown in Annex 3.
When the lamp is placed in the positions specified by the manufacturer, the angle of incidence of its light on the plate surface shall not exceed 82° at any point.
The registration plate lamp shall be designed so that no light is emitted directly towards the rear, except red light where the device is combined or grouped with a rear lamp.
The colour of light emitted by the registration plate lamp shall be sufficiently colourless not to cause any appreciable change in the colour of the registration plate.
The rear lighting assembly shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and the other markings defined in paragraphs 3.3.3.2. to 3.3.3.6.
All markings on the rear lighting assembly shall be clearly legible and indelible.
The approval marking applied to the rear lighting assembly shall have a character size "a" of at least 5 mm.
The approval marking of the assembly shall include the four to six-digit sequential approval number placed close to the approval mark.
The approval marking shall bear the symbols identifying the light signalling functions prescribed in paragraph 3.2.4., including MR, MS, 12 and LM1.
The approval marking shall include the number of this Regulation followed by the letter "R" and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force.
Where the lamp cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately, it shall bear a horizontal arrow showing the position in which it is to be mounted.
For the rear direction indicator lamp of category 12 and the rear position lamp, the horizontal arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle.
Where the assembly is mounted below 750 mm and has a reduced light distribution, a vertical arrow starting from a horizontal segment and directed downwards shall be marked.
The rear lighting assembly shall bear the approval marking.
The rear lighting assembly shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
Because the assembly contains non-replaceable light sources, it shall bear the marking of its rated voltage of 12 V.
The approval marking shall be placed on an inner or outer part of the lamp which is not designed to be separated from the transparent light-emitting part.
The approval marking shall be visible when the assembly is fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the boot lid is opened.
Where the outer lens is designed to be separated from the main body, the approval marking shall be placed on both the detachable lens and the main body.
Where a common outer lens is used for several devices with different approval markings, the main body of each device shall bear only the approval marking of its own function.
The approval marking and the trade name, light source, rated voltage and module markings shall be affixed on the lamp.

Where the functions of the assembly are grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated, a single approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number may be affixed anywhere on the assembly provided it is visible after installation.
No part of the grouped or combined assembly that transmits light shall be removable without at the same time removing the approval mark.
The size of the components of a single approval mark on the combined assembly shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks.
The rear lighting assembly shall be manufactured so that the minimum requirements for sampling by an inspector set forth in Annex 5 are complied with.
No measured value of the produced assembly shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the values prescribed in this Regulation.
For the registration plate lamp, the unfavourable deviation of the luminance gradient from 2.5 x Bo/cm shall be comparable to 20 per cent and from 3.0 x Bo/cm comparable to 30 per cent.
The rear direction indicator lamp of category 2 shall have minimum geometric visibility angles of 45° inboard and 80° outboard, and 15° above and below.
The single rear position lamp (MR) shall have minimum geometric visibility angles of 80° to each side and 15° above and 10° below the horizontal.
The single stop lamp (MS) shall have minimum geometric visibility angles of 45° to each side and 15° above and 10° below the horizontal.
Where the rear direction indicator, rear position or stop lamp is installed at a mounting height of 750 mm or less, the photometric intensity shall be verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.

Within the light distribution field, the light pattern shall be substantially uniform, with the intensity in each direction meeting at least the lowest minimum value shown on the surrounding grid lines.
For the registration plate lamp of category 1, the luminance measurement points shall be those defined for plate size 240 x 130 mm in Figure A3-XIV.
After the heat resistance test for the rear fog and daytime running function, no distortion, deformation, cracking or colour modification of the assembly shall be perceptible.

For the position, stop, direction indicator and registration plate functions using LED technology, the luminous intensities measured after 1 min and after 30 min of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
Operation of the direction indicator lamp during the photometric stability test shall be in flashing mode at f = 1.5 Hz with a duty factor of 50 per cent.
The registration plate illumination function shall be checked for compliance 4 seconds after switch-on at any measurement point given in Annex 3.
The rear direction indicator lamp of category 12 shall be checked for compliance 0.2 seconds after switch-on at the reference coordinate HV.
The rear position lamp shall be checked for compliance 4 seconds after switch-on at the reference coordinate HV.
The stop lamp shall be checked for compliance 0.2 seconds after switch-on at the reference coordinate HV.
The rear retro-reflector shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.

Where necessary to determine the angle of rotation unambiguously, the rear retro-reflector of Class IA or IB shall bear the word "TOP" inscribed horizontally on the highest part of its illuminating surface.
The approval marking or Unique Identifier and the markings of paragraph 3.3.4. shall be clearly legible on the rear retro-reflector.

Where the retro-reflector is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated with the signal lamps, a single approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number or Unique Identifier may be affixed.
No light-transmitting part of the grouped assembly shall be removable without at the same time removing the approval mark or Unique Identifier.
The size of the components of a single approval mark on the combined assembly shall not be less than the minimum required for the smallest of the individual marks.
The rear retro-reflector shall be so constructed that it functions satisfactorily and will continue to do so in normal use.
The rear retro-reflector shall not have any defect in design or manufacture detrimental to its efficient operation or to its maintenance in good condition.
The components of the rear retro-reflector shall not be capable of being easily dismantled.
The outer surface of the rear retro-reflector shall be easy to clean, not rough, and any protuberances shall not prevent easy cleaning.
When the rear retro-reflector is in normal use, there shall be no access to its inner surface.
Where the rear retro-reflector consists of a combined retro-reflecting optical unit and filter, they shall be designed so they cannot be separated under normal conditions of use.
The colouring of the retro-reflecting optical unit of the rear retro-reflector by means of paint or varnish shall not be permitted.
For the night-time colour test, the rear retro-reflector shall be illuminated by CIE Standard Illuminant A with an angle of divergence of 1/3° and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0°.
Where the retro-reflector is white, the trichromatic coordinates x and y of Standard Illuminant A shall not change by more than 0.01 after reflection by the device.
For the daytime colour test, the retro-reflective material shall be illuminated by CIE Standard Illuminant D65 using geometry (45a:0) or (0:45a).
Every rear retro-reflector of Class IA or IB shall meet the photometric and colorimetric requirements of paragraphs 5.1.4. to 5.1.5.
Ten samples of the rear retro-reflector shall be tested in the chronological order indicated in paragraph 5.1.7.
The ten retro-reflector samples shall be subjected to the heat resistance test of Annex 6 Part 1 and, at least one hour after, examined as to their colorimetric characteristics and RI.
The first group of two retro-reflector samples shall be subjected successively to the water penetration test and then, if satisfactory, to the resistance to fuels and lubricants tests.
The second group of two retro-reflector samples shall be subjected to the corrosion test and then to the abrasive-strength test of the rear face.
The fourth group of two retro-reflector samples shall be subjected to the resistance to weathering test of Annex 6 Part 6.
The rear retro-reflector shall be specified with one or more reference axes corresponding to the illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° in the table of RI values.
For photometric measurement, the illuminating surface of the Class IA or IB retro-reflector shall be limited to 100 cm2 within a circle of 200 mm diameter.
The red rear retro-reflector of Class IA or IB shall achieve an RI of at least 3.00·102 mcd·lx-1 at 20' divergence for β1 = 0°, β2 = 0°, and at least 2.00·102 and 1.00·102 mcd·lx-1 at ±10° and ±20°.
The red rear retro-reflector of Class IA or IB shall achieve an RI of at least 5·100 mcd·lx-1 at 1°30' divergence for β1 = 0°, β2 = 0°, and at least 2.8·100 and 2.5·100 mcd·lx-1 at ±10° and ±20°.
Where the Class IA or IB retro-reflector is installed with its H plane at a mounting height less than 750 mm above the ground, the RI values shall be verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
The trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous flux of the rear retro-reflector shall be within the night-time red limits specified in UN Regulation No. 48.
The rear retro-reflector shall be subjected to a heat test of 48 hours at 65 °C ± 2 °C with subsequent visual inspection for distortion.
The rear retro-reflector shall be subjected to a water test of 10 minutes in normal position and 10 minutes in inverted position, followed by visual inspection.
The rear retro-reflector shall be subjected to a motor fuel resistance test of 5 minutes followed by visual inspection.
The rear retro-reflector shall be subjected to a lubricating oil resistance test of 5 minutes followed by visual inspection.
The rear retro-reflector shall be subjected to a corrosion test of 24 hours, a 2-hour interval and a further 24 hours, followed by visual inspection.
The rear face of the retro-reflector shall be subjected to the abrasive-strength test for 1 minute followed by visual inspection.
The shape of the illuminating surface of the Class IA or IB retro-reflector shall not be easily confused with the triangular shape from an observation distance of 10 metres.
The moulded plastics retro-reflector shall be kept for 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at 65 °C ± 2 °C and then cooled for 1 hour at 23 °C ± 2 °C.
After the heat resistance test, no cracking or appreciable distortion of the retro-reflector or of its optical component shall be visible.

The retro-reflector shall be immersed for 10 minutes in water at 50 °C ± 5 °C with the highest point of its illuminating surface 20 mm below the water surface, and the test repeated after turning it through 180°.
After the water penetration test, no water shall have penetrated to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit.

The retro-reflector combined with a light shall be stripped of all removable parts and subjected to a saline mist for 50 hours, comprising two 24-hour exposure periods separated by a 2-hour drying interval.
Immediately after the corrosion test, the retro-reflector shall not show signs of excessive corrosion liable to impair its efficiency.
The retro-reflector samples shall be exposed to accelerated artificial weathering in accordance with EN ISO 4892-2:2013 using the parameters of Table A6-1.
The retro-reflective device shall be exposed to the accelerated weathering test for a period of 500 hours.
The outer surface and illuminating surface of the retro-reflector shall be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in a mixture of 70 vol. per cent n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent toluol.
About five minutes after the fuel mixture is applied, the surface of the retro-reflector shall show no apparent surface changes except slight surface cracks.
The outer and illuminating surface of the retro-reflector shall be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in detergent lubricating oil and, after about 5 minutes, cleaned before the RI is measured.
For the Class IVA type impact test, a 13 mm diameter polished solid steel ball shall be dropped once vertically onto the central part of the lens from a height of 0.76 m.

The rear lighting and retro-reflector assembly shall be fitted on the vehicle so that, in normal conditions of use and notwithstanding vibrations, it retains the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation.
The lamps of the rear assembly shall be fitted so that they cannot be inadvertently maladjusted.
When fitted to the vehicle, the reference axis of each rear light-signalling lamp shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road.
The reference axis of each rear light-signalling device shall be parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±3° in each direction.
Lamps of the rear assembly constituting a pair shall be mounted symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle.
Lamps of the rear assembly constituting a pair shall have identical nominal photometric characteristics.
Lamps of the rear assembly constituting a pair shall come on and go off simultaneously.

The photometric and colorimetric requirements of each function of the assembly shall be fulfilled when all other functions with which it is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated are switched off.
The stop lamp and the rear direction indicator lamp shall not be reciprocally incorporated with one another.

Where the stop lamp and direction indicator lamp are grouped, any horizontal or vertical straight line through the projections of their apparent surfaces shall not intersect more than two borderlines separating adjacent areas of different colour.

Where the rear lamp is a single lamp composed of distinct parts, either the parts shall occupy at least 60 per cent of the circumscribing quadrilateral or the minimum distance between facing edges shall not exceed 75 mm.
No rear lamp of the assembly other than the direction indicator lamp shall be a flashing lamp.
No red light which could give rise to confusion shall be emitted from the rear position lamp or stop lamp in a forward direction.
No white light which could give rise to confusion shall be emitted from the registration plate lamp in a rearward direction.
The red rear position and stop lamps shall not be directly visible to an observer moving in zone 1 of a transverse plane situated 25 m forward of the foremost point of the vehicle.

The electrical connection of the rear position lamp and the rear registration plate illuminating device shall be such that they cannot be switched on or off otherwise than simultaneously with the front position lamp.
Where the rear lamp is an interdependent lamp system, all its light sources shall be switched on and off simultaneously.
The colour of the light emitted by the rear registration plate lamp shall be white.
The colour of the rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be red.
No obstacle shall lie inside the angles of geometric visibility of any rear lamp that prevents the propagation of light from any part of its apparent surface observed from infinity.
Where any part of the apparent surface of a rear lamp is hidden by vehicle parts, proof shall be furnished that the unhidden part still conforms to the photometric values prescribed for approval.
Where the rear lamp is mounted below 750 mm above the ground, the photometric field of measurement of the installed optical unit may be reduced to 5° below the horizontal.
Where the rear lamp is an interdependent lamp system, the geometric visibility requirements shall be fulfilled when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.
The vehicle shall have two rear direction indicators approved as category 2 according to UN Regulation No. 6 or category 12 according to UN Regulation No. 148.
The clearance between the inner edges of the two rear direction indicator illuminating surfaces shall be at least 180 mm.
The rear direction indicator lamps shall be mounted at a height of not less than 350 mm and not more than 1,200 mm above the ground.
The forward distance between the centre of reference of the rear indicators and the rearmost transverse plane of the vehicle shall not exceed 300 mm.
The rear direction indicators shall have horizontal geometric visibility angles of 20° inwards and 80° outwards.
The rear direction indicators shall have vertical geometric visibility of 15° above and below, reduced to 5° below where mounted below 750 mm.
The rear direction indicator lamps shall switch on independently of the other lamps, and all indicators on one side shall be switched on and off by means of one control.

The mandatory direction indicator operating tell-tale shall, if optical, be a flashing green lamp that is extinguished, remains alight without flashing or shows a marked frequency change on indicator failure.
The rear direction indicator light flashing frequency shall be 90 ± 30 times per minute.
Operation of the direction indicator control shall be followed within not more than 1 second by the appearance of the light and within not more than 1.5 seconds by its first extinction.
In the event of failure, other than a short circuit, of one direction indicator lamp, the other lamps indicating the same direction shall continue to flash or remain alight.
The stop lamp shall be mounted at a height of not less than 250 mm and not more than 1,500 mm above the ground.
The stop lamp shall be mounted at the rear of the vehicle.
The stop lamp shall have a horizontal geometric visibility of 45° to left and right as a single lamp, or 45° outwards and 10° inwards for each pair of lamps.
All stop lamps shall light up simultaneously when the braking system provides the braking signal defined in UN Regulation No. 78.
The vehicle shall have one rear registration plate illuminating device approved as category 2 according to UN Regulation No. 50 or 148.
The rear registration plate illuminating device shall be arranged such that it illuminates the space reserved for the registration plate.
The rear registration plate illuminating device shall be positioned in width such that it illuminates the space reserved for the registration plate.

Where the registration plate lamp is combined with the rear position lamp or reciprocally incorporated in the stop lamp, its photometric characteristics may be modified during illumination of the stop lamp.
The rear position lamp shall be mounted at a height of not less than 250 mm and not more than 1,500 mm above the ground.
The rear position lamp shall be mounted at the rear of the vehicle.
The rear position lamp shall have a horizontal geometric visibility of 80° to left and right as a single lamp, or 80° outwards and 20° inwards for each pair.
The rear position lamp shall be oriented rearwards.

Where the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a direction indicator, the rear position lamp on that side may be switched off during the entire ON and OFF cycle of the direction indicator.
The vehicle shall have one or two rear retro-reflectors type-approved as Class IA or IB according to UN Regulation No. 3 or UN Regulation No. 150.
The rear retro-reflector shall be mounted at a height of not less than 250 mm and not more than 900 mm above the ground.
The rear retro-reflector shall have a horizontal geometric visibility of 30° to left and right as a single reflector, or 30° outwards and 10° inwards for each pair of reflectors.
The rear retro-reflector shall be oriented rearwards.

The rear assembly shall be designed so that the direction indicator lamp and stop lamp are not reciprocally incorporated, while grouping is permitted only subject to the borderline rule of paragraph 5.6.1.3.
The rear position lamp shall be switched on when the daytime running lamps of the vehicle are switched on.
The measured geometric visibility angles of the installed rear lamps shall fulfil the individual specifications, with an allowance of ±3° as permitted in paragraph 5.3.
The presence, number, colour, arrangement and category of the rear lamps shall be checked by visual inspection of the lamps and their markings.

The electronic drive board of the rear lighting assembly shall be designed so that radiated or conducted disturbances do not cause incorrect operation of the direction indicators, stop lamp or rear position lamp.
The electronic control/drive board submitted as an ESA shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's trade name or mark and the type designation.
The electronic drive assembly approved as an ESA shall bear the approval mark described in paragraph 5.3.
The EMC approval mark of the electronic drive assembly shall comprise a circle containing the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the approving country.
The EMC approval mark shall include the number of this Regulation followed by "R", a dash and the approval number to the right of the circle.
The EMC approval marking on the electronic drive assembly need not be visible when the ESA is installed in the vehicle.

The electronic drive board and harness of the rear lighting assembly shall be designed, constructed and fitted so that the vehicle complies with the EMC requirements of this Regulation in normal conditions of use.
The electronic drive assembly of the rear lighting shall be tested for radiated and conducted emissions and for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.
The broadband radiated emissions of the ESA shall not exceed 62 to 52 dBµV/m in the 30 to 75 MHz band, decreasing logarithmically, and 52 to 63 dBµV/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band.
The broadband radiated emissions of the ESA shall remain below a constant limit of 63 dBµV/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz band.
The narrowband radiated emissions of the ESA shall not exceed 52 to 42 dBµV/m in the 30 to 75 MHz band and 42 to 53 dBµV/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band.
The narrowband radiated emissions of the ESA shall remain below a constant limit of 53 dBµV/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz band.
The transient conducted disturbances emitted by the ESA on the 12 V supply lines shall not exceed a pulse amplitude of +75 V positive and -100 V negative.
The ESA shall withstand, in over 90 per cent of the 20 MHz to 2 GHz band, test levels of 60 V/m stripline, 75 V/m TEM cell, 60 mA BCI, 30 V/m ALSE and 21 V/m reverberation chamber.
The ESA shall withstand, over the whole 20 MHz to 2 GHz band, a minimum test level of 50 V/m stripline, 62.5 V/m TEM cell, 50 mA BCI, 25 V/m ALSE and 18 V/m reverberation chamber.
The ESA shall withstand, in over 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz band, test levels of 10 V/m in the ALSE and 7 V/m in the reverberation chamber.
During the immunity tests, the ESA shall show no degradation of performance of the immunity related functions, including the correct operation of the direction indicators and stop lamp.
The ESA shall withstand test pulse 1 of -75 V applied for 500 pulses with functional performance status class III.
The ESA shall withstand test pulse 2a of +37 V applied for 500 pulses with functional performance status class I.
The ESA shall withstand test pulse 3a of -112 V applied for 1 hour with functional performance status class I.
The ESA shall withstand test pulse 3b of +75 V applied for 1 hour with functional performance status class I.
The ESA which shall be operational during engine start phases shall withstand the starting profile with 10 pulses at test level II.
The ESA shall withstand test pulse 2b of +10 V applied for 10 pulses with functional performance status class II.
Where the electronic drive assembly does not include an electronic oscillator above 9 kHz, it shall be deemed to comply with the narrowband limits of paragraph 6.6.2. and Annex 8.
Where the rear lighting ESA contains no switches and no inductive load, it shall be deemed to comply with the transient conducted emission requirement without testing.
